value.description: What is the temperature supported by the Solidigm SSD 660p Series 512 GB, and is it necessary to add a cooling solution to the SSD?
value.content:
To find the supported temperature on an SSD follow these steps: 

 

  1. Go to the product specification page (ARK). 

  1. Search for the desired product. 

  1. Once the product is found, access it. 

  1. Under Reliability is the Operating Temperature (Maximum) and Operating Temperature (Minimum). 

 

It is not necessary to have a cooling solution system just for the SSD. If a system comes with a cooling solution system for the SSD or has the option to install one, it can be integrated. 

Heat generated depends more on the form factor from the system if it is too close or small that it does not allow proper airflow. 

Here is some additional information: 

 

If I don't have a thermal solution on my Solidigm® SSD M.2 device, is there an impact? 

Without a thermal solution, it's possible to experience a performance impact if the device reaches a temperature of 80° C (throttle set point). At this temperature, the device will limit its performance to prevent overheating. 

The SSD won't be damaged as the throttle set point has been reached. However, the built-in thermal throttle safety feature that prevents damage can result in significantly lower performance or shutdown. 

 

A thermal solution came with my motherboard. Can I use that one? 

Yes, under heavy sustained storage workloads these thermal solutions may extend the time for the SSD to reach its thermal throttle set point. Although Solidigm hasn't validated these thermal solutions to deliver the same level of sustained performance as the solution provided by Solidigm, any thermal solution will provide some benefit. Results may vary based on the efficacy of the solution.

Exothermic Event
An exothermic event exhibited by any Intel server product wil receive a full failure analysis by Intel.  An exothermic event is defined as a damage to any component(s) or circuitry found on an Intel product where overheating, smoke or flaming has occurred.  The failure analysis is limited to the original Intel only product that has not been modified/customized with changes not approved by Intel, and does not include failure analysis to or caused by non-Intel add-in peripherals and add-in cards. Intel requests that the complete system remain intact and un-energized going forward (non-compliance will not cause the analysis to be rejected but can aid in identifying the fault)."
Manufacturing Defects
Re-occurring manufacturing defects on common product will receive failure analysis by Intel Engineering / Manufacturing teams. Examples of manufacturing defects may include, but are not limited to, the following:
Loose / unattached components found within the system
Incorrect component placement
Incorrect or missing components
Cosmetic damage outside of Intel quality standards
Presence of foreign material within the system"
Systemic Failures

Failure is reproducible on multiple systems (3 minimum) under normal operational conditions. Thorough customer site/remote troubleshooting has been performed with an Intel support representative, producing complete error logs, failure details and detailed steps for issue reproduction in an Intel lab.   • A common issue (issue with identical failure symptoms) does not exhibit itself on multiple Intel product of the same type (minimum of 3) Intel will not do FA on a single, one-off failure.
  • This will must to be a trend of the same type of issue, for example a minimum of 3 same type of issues from a same purchase order but not from a period longer than 3 months.
  • Full troubleshooting of the issue was not performed with an Intel support representative
  • Full failure details and error logs were not provided to Intel.  
  • Failure details include:
    • Full and complete system configuration details
    • Complete description of failure
    • Complete steps used to reproduce the issue
    • Steps taken to troubleshoot and narrow the issue down to a specific Intel product or component
  • Issue was NOT reproducible when all of the following non-Intel THOL configuration variables were removed
    • Add-in cards
    • Peripherals
    • Firmware
    • Hardware Drivers
  • The original Intel product was modified / customized with non-Intel approved changes.  Examples of such changes may include, and are not limited to the following:
    •  Custom firmware installed to any component
    •  Custom BMC
    •  Custom BIOS
    •  Circuitry / On-board component changes
    •  Custom system interface boards
    •  Other system components
Exceptions:
Upon occasion, an exception to this policy may be granted to assist customers with debug of 3rd party peripherals or custom embedded designs.

Category & Issue selection plays a vital role in segmentation of service and warranty tickets. They evolve through time to capture known and potential issues keeping products and services in mind, and also to keep accuracy and relevance.

Important notes

  • C&I selection must be based on root cause and not on symptoms.
  • C&I selection must be updated as needed during ticket handling time to accurately reflect the root cause.
  • If service ticket turns into warranty ticket, C&I must be updated if applicable: OEM replacement, refund, secure return, dead on arrival, etc.

Why do we care about C&Is?

  • Helps segment both service and warranty tickets by root cause.
  • Helps identify systematic issues with products and support services.
  • Helps identify top issues.

Please use this guide to determine appropriate Category & Issue (C&I) selection for each ticket under SSDs & Memory products. Contact your SME or PSE for any questions/concerns.

Starting December 2021, the C&I selection has been divided by product groups based on the product hierarchy:

  1. There are options defined at the product level 1 (Memory and Storage) that are shared with all products at level 2 and level 3.
  2. In a similar way, there are specific C&I options defined at the product level 2 (Client SSD, Data Center SSD, Intel Optane Memory, Intel Optane Persistent Memory and SSD Software) that are shared only with the products at level 3 under each product level 2 group respectively.
Memory and Storage

These C&I are visible to all products under Memory and Storage.

Customer did not understand documentation Customer read the documentation but misunderstood what it stated Customer needed guidance to help them follow steps/instructions in a guide.  (Note: this may be followed up be a CX to help improve the article/document)

Request for NDA Materials, such as the Product Specifications Customers requesting material that is under NDA Use Full Product spec C&I if customer is requesting Full product spec.

Performance/Benchmark Settings Issue Specifically a case where the user does not have their configuration setup properly to test performance Customer is trying to measure performance with a specific benchmark and are getting 'bad' results.  The Root cause is that they did not have the proper settings in the benchmark to test performance on a given drive(s)

How to respond to California Prop 65 Inquiries and Requests

(Applicable to All Intel Products)

 

Scenario 1: Respond with below text for general Prop 65 questions or for inquiries regarding if and how Intel demonstrates Prop65 compliance.

" Thank you for your inquiry. Intel is committed to protecting the environment and complying with all health, safety, and hazardous substance laws and regulations.

The Safe Drinking Water and Toxic Enforcement Act of 1986, known as Proposition 65, was adopted as a voter initiative in November 1986. Proposition 65 requires California to publish a list of chemicals known in the State of California to cause cancer and/or reproductive harm. The list, updated annually, has grown to include approximately 900 chemicals, including a wide range of naturally occurring and synthetic chemicals that include additives or ingredients in pesticides, common household products, food, drugs, dyes, or solvents. Proposition 65 requires businesses to provide a “clear and reasonable” warning before knowingly and intentionally exposing any customer in California to a listed chemical if the exposure exceeds certain thresholds established by the law.

Intel includes the warning label when necessary to comply with Proposition 65 and to inform customers that the product contains one or more chemicals on the State’s list."

  1. Process_WW_Case Handling Guidelines for IOG (Intel Optane Group) and NPSG (NAND Product & Solutions Group) [UPDATED]

Special Guidelines for SSDs & Memory Products

Non-Supported Environments (Consumer-Data Center)

When the customer uses the following SSD models in a non-supported environment and a warranty is required, the agents can process the warranty without escalating the case the PSE level for approval.

Educate the customer by mentioning the following: “Please be aware that you are using the drive in a non-supported environment and it may cause the SSD to fail sooner than expected because of the workload” and then proceed with the RMA. 

Intel SSD 525 Series Intel SSD 540s Series Intel SSD Pro 2500 Series
Intel SSD 530 Series Intel SSD 600p Series Intel SSD Pro 5400s Series
Intel SSD 535 Series Intel SSD Pro 1500 Series Intel SSD Pro 6000p Series

Note: For any other drive being misused, the agents must still escalate to PSE level for approval (for example: Intel® SSD 545s Series, Intel® SSD Pro 5450s Series, etc.).

Go to Index  

NUC Scope vs SSD/Optane Scope

For any issue with an Intel® NUC (Mini-PC, Kit, Board), the case product will be the NUC product, the support will be provided by the NUC supporting team, and if needed; they will follow the NUC product escalation path for any support or issues. The NUC PSE/BU will reach out to other product PSEs if needed for specific features/support (i.e.: AMT. VPRO/Graphics, Wireless, etc.).

The only exception would be if the NUC supporting team determines after doing some troubleshooting that the issue is specific to an Intel® SSD/Intel® Optane™ product in a NUC Kit or Board. If so, they will transfer the case to the SSDs & Memory supporting teams under the specific Intel® SSD/Intel® Optane™ product for proper support.

If the NUC case is received by the SSDs & Memory supporting teams, they can try (to reduce customer effort) to help the customer by following the below recommendations, however it is important to educate the customer that the technical support specifically for NUCs is provided by a different team, so that in an eventual scenario where the SSDs & Memory supporting teams have to transfer the case to the NUC supporting team, the customer is aware of the reason why the support ticket is being transferred.

  • Compatibility questions: Use the Intel Compatibility Tool to check if the Intel® SSD is officially supported by the customer's NUC model. This will avoid the SSDs & Memory supporting teams to transfer the ticket to the NUC supporting team, and will reduce the time to provide support if the SSDs & Memory supporting teams identify the problem is related to the SSD itself.
  • Recognition questions: The SSDs & Memory supporting teams can ask the customers (if it is possible for them) to test the SSD in a non-NUC system to verify the SSD functionality. This approach will help to reduce the time to provide support if the SSDs & Memory supporting teams identify the problem is related to the SSD itself.

Go to Index  

RST Scope vs SSD/Optane Scope

The new Intel® Optane™ Memory and Storage Management application available from the Microsoft* store is a new tool used to setup and configure the Intel® Optane™ memory as well as to setup and manage Intel® RST RAID. Since the same application works for Intel® Optane™ memory as well as for Intel® RST RAID setups, the SSDs & Memory supporting teams must be able to determine the nature of the customers' issues to accurately route the customers to the RST supporting team if needed, or handle the cases themselves.

When the customers come to the SSDs & Memory supporting teams with a configuration/issue that includes and involves the legacy Intel® RST app, the legacy Intel® Optane™ app or the new Intel® Optane™ Memory and Storage Management app from Microsoft* store, the SSDs & Memory supporting teams must follow the criteria below:

  1. If the issue is related to the Intel® Optane™ memory, the IOG supporting team should own the case and work on it.
  2. If the issue is related to an Intel® SSD, the SSDs & Memory supporting teams should transfer the case to the RST supporting team, unless the issue seems to be a hardware related issue. In that scenario, the SSDs & Memory supporting teams (NPSG or IOG depending on the SSD type) should own the case and work on it.
  3. If the issue is related to non Intel® SSD, the SSDs & Memory supporting teams should transfer the case to the RST supporting team.

If the SSDs & Memory supporting teams determine the customer's issue is within the SSDs & Memory supporting teams scope, update the product accordingly (use the Intel® SSD or the Intel® Optane™ product that the customer has) and take ownership of the case. On the other hand, if the customer's issue is under the RST supporting team scope, update the product to Intel® Rapid Storage Technology (Intel® RST) and transfer the customer to the support channels available for the RST supporting team (Web Ticketing and Communities). 

Note: The detailed process of transferring a case to the RST supporting team as well as the support channels available for Intel® RST are explained in the article Process_WW_Intel_Rapid_Storage Technology_Support_Guidelines.

Go to Index  

EOIS vs OEM Scenario

There are some uncommon cases where the customer has an OEM drive that is also an EOIS product. In such scenarios, the agents must follow the EOIS process described in the article Process_WW_EOIS Support Plan for Contact Centers, and also add a new line to let the customer know that they have an OEM drive so they may want to also contact the OEM for assistance. The highlighted text below is the extra line the agents should add to their communication with the customers:

“Intel Customer Service no longer responds to telephone, chat, or e-mail inquiries for [Product Name] but you may want to try our Intel Community forums to get recommendations from fellow community members. You may also find the Discontinued Products website helpful to address your request.

Please consider as well that your product is an OEM unit. An OEM unit is a product with customized features and firmware developed by the OEM. For this reason, you may also want to contact the OEM directly for additional information about your request."

Use the following closing reason for the case: Transferred to OEM/Place of Purchase.

Note: If the product is not OEM (just EOIS), then follow the article Process_WW_EOIS Support Plan for Contact Centers as usual.

Go to Index  

Remote Assistance

The SSDs & Memory supporting teams have the option to perform remote sessions to assist customers and to help them to solve the issues in a quick and easy way. The remote session option is another resource the agents have in order to assist the customers, and it should be used when the agents consider it is necessary to resolve the issue in a faster way and to reduce the customer effort during the process.

The primary scenario to use remote assistance due to the trobleshooting complexity is for chat cases about Intel® Optane™ memory configuration and setup. However, remote assistance can also be used for other scenarios and products.

Note: Complete details about the process, notes and key messages are included in the article Process_WW_Intel Remote Assistance Tool (LogMeIn) Support.

Go to Index  

Sending Defective Units to PSE

When a defective unit must be sent to a PSE for further investigation, the agents must inform the Warranty Team in their Contact Centers so they can assist with the process. The agents must confirm the following information so that the Warranty Team can proceed accordingly:

  • The PSE that will receive the unit.
  • The PSE email.
  • The PSE shipping address.

Note: By default PSEs do not receive defective units, however there may be special cases where the Business Unit (BU) wants to further investigate a failing unit. PSEs will properly inform the SMEs when this is the case. 

Go to Index  

RMA Cases from IPS/Community Cases

When handling a case from IPS or Community that requires an RMA to be resolved, a new case must be created (clone case) to perform the RMA process. This new case must have as case origin Internal (not IPS or Community). Communications with the customers will continue over the original case.

For Community cases only: In case the customer reports an issue in the forum and the agent concludes the SSD is defective and needs replacement, contact the customer over email to get the required details for the RMA, and post a response in the forum that let the customer know he/she will be contacted over email.

Go to Index  

Inventory/Substitution Lookup

Key Considerations

  • The terminology used for this guideline is the following:
  1. Original SSD: The original drive the customer has (same model).
  2. Substitute SSD: The approved substitute SSD for the original SSD model. This is the model listed in the substitute matrix.
  3. Alternate SSD: Another SSD model that may also work as a suitable equivalent part to the customer's original SSD, but it is not listed in the substitute matrix as an official substitute. The alternate SSD is found in a case basis to help customers getting a replacement unit.
  • This guideline is only to find the proper alternate parts for the customers' drives by doing an extra effort to allocate a suitable part and avoid the customer entering into a cumbersome refund process.
  • For units (original, substitute or alternate) in backorder, low stock quantities and refund, please keep referring to the process described in the article Process_WW_Planner Escalations Handling Guide.

Guideline

When a new warranty request is received and has been validated by the agents, the proper replacement unit has to be found by following these steps:

  1. Inventory availability: The agents have to check if the customer’s SSD is available in inventory, or on the other hand, if an approved substitute is available. If the same SSD that the customer has is available, then the warranty order is placed; otherwise, the agents have to inform the customer that the available option is a substitute SSD (if any) and get the customer’s confirmation to set up the warranty order.
    • Do not commit with the substitute SSD as the customer may still get the original SSD as replacement. Instead, offer the substitute SSD as a possible option to receive since the stock for the original SSD is low.
  2. No inventory availability: If there is no stock for the original SSD nor the substitute SSD, the agents must escalate the case to the L2 Technical SME to look for an alternate part that could fulfill the customer’s needs. The L2 Technical SME will look for possible alternate SSDs and return the case to the L1 agent to inform the customer about the available options; and wait for the customer’s confirmation to proceed with the warranty order. The L1 agent has to also inform the customer about the ETA of the original SSD in case the customer prefers to wait for it. If the number of units in the request is more than 3 (4 or more), the L2 Technical SME has to escalate the request to the PSE with the alternate SSD options for approval. If the request is for 3 or less units, the L2 Technical SME provides the approval. In case there is no availability of alternate parts, then the agents have to offer a refund as the last option.
    • Do not commit with the alternate SSD as the customer may still get the original drive as replacement. Instead, offer the alternate SSD as a possible option to receive since the stock for the original SSD is low.
  3. No agreement from the customer: If the customer does not agree with the alternate options offered nor with the ETA of the original part, the agents have to offer the refund option as the only available option. 

Go to Index  

New Branding for 3D XPoint™

Note that as we move to distinguish our Intel® Optane™ products, we will no longer be referencing our “Optane” media as 3D XPoint™, but instead be using Intel® Optane™ memory media or Intel® Optane™ storage media. Although still legally valid, we want to continue to drive awareness and brand recognition of Intel® Optane™ technology.

You can find more information in the IOG Product Brand Quick Reference Guide site, or search the Intel - Names Database for correct product and technology usage.

Go to Index  

Availability of Product Specification Documents

The Business Unit (BU) has decided to stop publishing product specification documents on intel.com. This applies to both newly launching products and older products. Existing product specification documents will be removed from the support site and marketing page.

Product specification documents can be shared with customers under NDA. The product specification document and all text contained within it is classified as Intel Confidential and cannot be shared with customers unless they have an NDA. If any questions about specific information, please escalate the case for discussion to PSE level.

The product specification documents will be available at the Resource & Design Center site. The agents should contact their local SME for assistance, SMEs can access these documents. If the document is not there, escalate to PSE level.

Note: Product briefs are available in the public article Product Briefs for Intel® Solid State Drives and Modules.

Go to Index  

SA# Added to Client Retail Boxes

All future Client products going in to channel (starting Stony Beach) will have the SA# on both pretty box and disti box (brown box). This will allow customers to provide the SA# without removing the module or SSD from the system.

Note: Data Center SSDs do not have pretty boxes, and disti box won't have the SA# either. Customers with Data Center SSDs will still have to use the label on the drive to provide the SA#.

Go to Index  

RMA Instructions for Super Micro (LOEM) Customer Returns

The Business Unit (BU) put in a special rule that Super Micro Computer, Inc is an Local OEM (LOEM) and should be treated as an OEM for RMA purposes. Hence all customers who purchase from Super Micro are treated as OEM customers and should be referred to LOEM i.e. Super Micro Computer, Inc. 

Please note that when a customer says that they purchased their drives from Super Micro, the agents should refer them to their LOEM. If the customer insists and they do not want to go back to Super Micro, or Super Micro denied the RMA request, escalate to the PSE level.

Important: As of now, there is only one Super Micro customer called Equus that is exempted from going back to the LOEM as per BU/SMG Sales team's instructions. 

Go to Index  

RMA Instructions for SSDs Used in Liquid Immersion Cooling Systems

Intel will honor the RMA for all SSDs (Data Center and Client SSDs) used in Liquid Immersion Cooling Systems, as long as there is no damage to the drive. Warranty will be covered under normal Terms and Conditions.

In addition to commonly requested information such as S/N# and SA#, the agents should ask for system specific information and type of cooling liquid, use case etc. Agents should also ask for pictures to make sure there is no customer induced damage to the drive (look for burnt or corrosion marks on the drive).

Escalate to PSE level if there are any questions or need clarification.

Go to Index  

Encourage Customers to Contact Distis First for SSDs RMAs

If a customer who is requesting for an RMA purchased the drive in the last 30 days, encourage the customer to reach out to their disti/reseller or place of purchase to get warranty. If the customer approaches their disti/reseller, their order fulfilment could happen much more efficiently.

Note: We'll still honor the product's warranty, but if the purchase was done recently (last 30 days), the best first option for customers is to reach out to their disti/reseller.

Go to Index  

Companies' Requests About Being Added Into The Data Recovery Options Article

If a customer is requesting to be added into the article Data Recovery Options for Intel® SSDs, the supporting agents must explain to the customer that Intel is not adding new companies to the list on the support site at this time.

Go to Index  

Intel® Optane™ SSD DC P4801X Series: New Heat Spreader SKUs

The Intel® Optane™ SSD DC P4801X M.2 form factor has new SKUs with heat spreader included. Production parts will be available November 1st, 2019. Low volume is expected in the channel. SSD + integrated heat spreader are shipping together for the first time on this product. IOG supporting agents should take note for any RMA requests on the below SKUs. value.description: How to add the Microsoft* hotfix and modify the Windows* installation to boot using the Intel SSD 600p/6000p Series.
value.content:
Windows® 8.1 and 10 offer native support for NVMe* drives, in Windows* 7 this support was added at a later time via a Windows® Update. This means that the Windows* 7 installation will not detect the Intel® SSD 600p/6000p Series, at least not without some modifications.

Requirements:
  • Windows* 7 SP1 x64.iso
  • Windows® 10.iso (https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/software-download/windows10)
  • Microsoft* hotfixes (https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/kb/2990941 and https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/kb/3087873) (Hotfixes need to be requested in this page, currently link sent by Microsoft via email)
  • NTlite* (https://www.ntlite.com/download/)
  • 7-Zip* (http://www.7-zip.org)

Installing and booting Windows* 7 on these drives is not a simple process, as there is no driver, and a stand-alone driver is not provided by Microsoft*. There are two things that need to be done. First, modify the Windows® installation, so that Windows® will detect the drive once installed. We also need to use the Windows® 10 installation to install Windows* 7, so that the installation will detect the drive as well. Confused yet? Don't worry, we'll break it down step by step for you.

*Links to third party sites and references to third party trademarks are provided for convenience and illustrative purposes only. Unless explicitly stated, Intel® is not responsible for the contents of such links, and no third party endorsement of Intel® or any of its products is implied.

Getting things ready:

1. If you don't already have them, download the Windows* 7 and Windows 10 ISO files from the Microsoft* website. I saved these ISOs to "C:\Temp\Windows Images"
2. Mount the Windows* 7 ISO, copy all contents into our working folder. For this tutorial, we will be using "C:\Temp\Windows 7"
3. The Microsoft* Hotfixes you received in your email come in the form of self extracting applications. Extract both of these hotfixes. We will extract the contents into "C:\Temp\Hotfix"
4. Install the latest version of NTlite*
5. Install the latest version of 7-zip*

Applying the hotfixes to our Windows 7 Installation.

1. Run NTLite*. 
2. In the toolbar, click on Add and navigate where we copied the files from the Windows* 7 ISO. ("C:\Temp\Windows 7")
3. Open and choose "Select Folder"
4. You will now see two folders: your current windows® (under "Live Install") and the ISO folder. Open and choose the version you want to install, home, ultimate etc., and press load on the toolbar, or right click and select load. For this tutorial, we will install Windows* 7 Pro x64.
5. On the left of the screen there will now be several options, under "Integrate" click on "Updates".

6. On the toolbar click on Add, locate and add the hotfixes (Windows6.1-KB2990941-v3-x64.msu and Windows6.1-KB3087873-v2-x64.msu)
7. Go to Apply (left side of the window).

8. Select "Process" on the top toolbar to apply the hotfixes to the Windows* 7 installation.

9. Close NTlite*
10. Go to your Windows 7 working folder (C:\Temp\Windows 7) then go open the "EFI" folder, now the "Microsoft" folder, copy the boot folder one step up into the EFI folder, leaving it as C:\Temp\Windows 7\EFI\Boot

11. Go to your sources folder and locate install.wim, right click and under 7-Zip select "Open Archive"

12. Navigate to 1\Windows\Boot\EFI\ locate the "bootmgfw.efi". Right click and copy to the desktop. Close 7-zip

13. Go to your desktop, rename bootmgfw.efi to bootx64.efi
14. Move the renamed bootx64.efi file into C:\Temp\Windows 7\EFI\

15. Open your Windows® 10 image.
16. In the Windows 10 image, go to sources\ copy the Boot.wim and Setup.exe. Paste this files under the same folder in your Windows* 7 working folder ("C:\Temp\Windows 7\Sources\")


Option 1. USB Flash Drive.
1. Go to your Windows* 7 working folder, and copy all of the contents into an USB flash drive (UEFI formatted if needed)

Option 2. Create ISO, burn into a DVD
1. Run NTLite*
2. From the previous process you should be able to see the Windows* 7 installation that we worked on previously.
3. Right click the version of Windows we worked on, choose "Create ISO"
4. Select where you want the ISO to be saved, and a file name. Click ok, then select the ISO label. OK again.
5. Locate ISO once created, right click and choose "Burn Disk Image" or burn it using your DVD burning software of choice.

Below is information that can be used to respond to customers with questions about this issue.
Note: This article will be updated with new questions/answers as they become available.  Please escalate questions that cannot be answered by the information below

Background
On Monday, May 7, Microsoft posted an announcement online that Microsoft is blocking some systems with Intel® SSDs from receiving the Windows 10 April 2018 Update (also known as RS4). This is in response to systems with Intel® SSD 600p Series and Intel® SSD Pro 6000p Series experiencing issues that may cause the system to crash and enter a UEFI screen after reboot. .

Recommendation for users that have updated to the April update to rollback  to the Windows 10 Fall Creators update version 1709 by by pressing the F8 key during the boot process and selecting to restore the previous version of the OS

Please send any press inquiries to Read, Simon <simon.read@intel.com>

Q: Why is Microsoft blocking some systems with Intel® SSDs from receiving the Windows 10 April 2018 update?
A: Microsoft has temporarily paused the Windows 10 April 2018 Update (also known as RS4) on select devices with Intel® SSD 600p Series and Intel® SSD Pro 6000p Series due
to issues that may cause a system to crash and enter a UEFI screen after reboot.

Q. What Intel® SSDs are impacted by this block?
A. To date, Intel is aware that the block Microsoft implemented for the Windows 10 April 2018 Update applies only to the Intel® SSD 600p Series and Intel® SSD Pro 6000p Series.

Q. Are Intel® Optane™ SSDs impacted by Microsoft’s decision to block the update?
A. We are unaware of any impact of this block on Intel® Optane™ SSDs.

Q. Have any end-users been impacted by this update block?
A. To date, we have received a minimal number of reported incidents.

Q. Is Microsoft working on a solution?
A. Yes, Microsoft is working on a resolution that will allow the April 2018 Update on these devices in the near future.

How to request EAC certs (Eurasian Certificates of Conformity) documents

 
No NDA required. Applicable to all Intel® Products Families
 

  • Purpose:  The purpose of this document is to describe the high-level process on how to manage customer request support of Eurasian Certificates of Conformity (EAC CoC) documentation.  Certificate of Conformity is a document stating compliance of a product to relevant Eurasian (Russia, Kazakhstan, Belarus, Armenia, Kyrgyzstan) standards and Directives (Safety/EMC/RoHS and etc). Compliance to those standards is confirmed by associated testing on that product.

 

  • Scope:  The scope of this document applies to the business process when searching Eurasian (Customs Union and Russia in particular) Certificate of Conformity (EAC) documentation.

 

  • Intel does not provide EAC documentation for pre-release products, engineering samples, or non-revenue product.  Additionally, Intel does not support products in “retired” status as these parts are not active, no longer being manufactured, or purchased and no inventory is available.

 
 
 

  • Search EAC certificate via External Website Support:

 

  • EAC CoC documentation can be easily found at our external (www.intel.com/rcis-certs ) website. Please note that Intel provides certificates only to specific product types which require it by the law.
  • From www.intel.com/rcis-certs in the Russia/Eurasian Economic Union column find Product Type, find needed Product in the list and click Download in the same row.
  • Please complete the steps above prior to proceeding further.
  • If the above process steps does not result a positive experience, escalate to PSE.

 
Scenario:

Find CoC documentation www.intel.com/rcis-certs
Document Selection Find needed CoC in the list and click Download in the same row.
If DoC is resulted Search positive, no further support is required
 
If DoC is not resulted
 		 Case#1:
Page/site unavailable (technical issue) - escalate to PSE need to contact IT TAC
If DoC is not resulted Case#2: Document not available
1.  Ask the customer to provide MM number or Product code of the product. Then go to Mark.intel.com and enter the MM# or product code provided by the customer. If the customer cannot provide requested information no further action can be taken.   Escalate to PSE.
2.  Enter MM number/Product code under search specification. In Mark status code needs to be AC.  i.e. active.  If not CoC has likely not been available. In that case inform customer that:
Intel does not provide EAC CoC documentation for pre-release products, engineering samples, or non-revenue product.  Additionally, Intel does not support products in “retired” status as these parts are not active, no longer being manufactured, or purchased and no inventory is available.  ESCALATE TO PSE if customer insists on this information.
3. If Product is appears as Active and no CoC available. ESCALATE TO PSE
If DoC is not resulted Special Cases:
Some specific questions for product types may happen:
  1. Processors:
    1. Cannot find CoC for any CPU: CPUs are not in scope of Eurasian technical regulations for Safety/EMC, so it is not required.
  2. Servers:
    1. Cannot find CoC for specific product code. Example: product code R1304WFXXX.  Need to refer to relevant Server Family CoC (Rr1000);
 
Use matrix below to identify Family name and cert applicable.
 
Example:
 
Provided product code is R1304WFXXX.
Second symbol “1” in that code refers to the server size -1U
First letter acronym symbols in the middle of the code refer to Platform name – WF (“Wolf Pass”).
Selecting 1U and WF gives Rr.
That means Rr1000 certificate should be provided to the customer.

value.content:
This is an internal process article. DO NOT attach to a case!
Attach the appropriate article that captures and solves the customer’s issue.
 
 
Key Consideration:
The following guidelines define how the teams supporting SSDs and Memory products can identify their specific covered products, and how these support tickets must be handled across the different levels of the ICS Memory and Storage queue. The support teams are still expected to follow the general case handling guidelines from the Process_WW_Case Handling General Guidelines article.
 
 
Intel Optane Group (IOG) and NAND Product & Solutions Group (NPSG)
The Intel Optane Group (IOG) was created after the Non-Volatile Memory Solutions Group (NSG) segmentation between Optane™ technology and NAND technology. IOG will be part of the Data Platforms Group (DPG), and will cover all products based on Optane™ technology as well as the SSD Software products that were under NSG before.
 
The NAND technology products on the other hand, will be covered by the new NAND Product & Solutions Group (NPSG), and will include only the Client and Data Center SSDs portfolio based on NAND technology.

How to identify the technology used by the SSD?

ISvC Custom Views Setup
Because all SSDs & Memory products share the same queue (ICS Memory and Storage), it is highly recommended that all agents, SMEs and PSEs supporting IOG and NPSG products create a custom view within ISvC to see only the products under their scope.
  • Note: While having a custom view setup is not really needed, it will help the agents, SMEs and PSEs to easily identify their covered products in a daily basis. Without these custom views, the agents, SMEs or PSEs will have to manually check and pickup the cases from the default ICS Memory and Storage queues.
Follow the below steps to create the required custom view for your product support scope.
 
IOG Custom View Setup
  1. Within ISvC, go to the Cases tab.
    •  
  2. Select the queue ICS Memory and Storage L1. If you don't have this queue option listed, you may need to request access to it.
  3. Clone the default ICS Memory and Storage L1 queue.
  4. Change the name of the new custom view to IOG ICS Memory and Storage L1 and save the new custom view. For SMEs who usually work on the level 2 and PSEs who usually work on level 3 or higher, specify the respective level in the name, for example: IOG ICS Memory and Storage L2 SME, IOG ICS Memory and Storage L3 GEO PSE, IOG ICS Memory and Storage L4 WW PSE or IOG ICS Memory and Storage L5 BU.
  5. Update the filters for the new view according to the following instructions:
    1. Depending on your role (agent, SME or PSE), you may need to update the top filter Filter by Owner to the proper level, for example ICS Memory and Storage L2 SME.
    2. Add a new filter for Product that contains the word Optane.
    3. Add a new filter for VPH NAV L2 that is equal to the string SSD Software.
    4. Add the following filter logic: 1 AND 2 AND (3 OR 4).
    5. Click the Save button.
  6. The new custom view for IOG is ready. Check that all products under the Product column are indeed products under the IOG scope only.

Note: This new custom view will behave just as the default ICS Memory and Storage L1 queue. With the above process, we are adding a second layer to filter by the desired products (the IOG products). 

NPSG Custom View Setup
  1. Within ISvC, go to the Cases tab.
  2. Select the queue ICS Memory and Storage L1. If you don't have this queue option listed, you may need to request access to it.
  3. Clone the default ICS Memory and Storage L1 queue.
  4. Change the name of the new custom view to NPSG ICS Memory and Storage L1. For SMEs who usually work on the level 2 and PSEs who usually work on level 3 or higher, specify the respective level in the name, for example: NPSG ICS Memory and Storage L2 SME, NPSG ICS Memory and Storage L3 GEO PSE, NPSG ICS Memory and Storage L4 WW PSE or NPSG ICS Memory and Storage L5 BU.
  5. Update the filters for the new view according to the following instructions:
    1. Depending on your role (agent, SME or PSE), you may need to update the top filter Filter by Owner to the proper level, for example ICS Memory and Storage L2 SME.
    2. Add a new filter for Product that does not contain the word Optane.
    3. Add a new filter for VPH NAV L2 that is not equal to the string SSD Software.
    4. Click the Save button.
  6. The new custom view for NPSG is ready. Check that all products under the Product column are indeed products under the NPSG scope only.

Note: This new custom view will behave just as the default ICS Memory and Storage L1 queue. With the above process, we are adding a second layer to filter by the desired products (the NPSG products). 

Routing Guidelines
When a new SSDs & Memory case arrives, it will end up in the default ICS Memory and Storage L1 queue. The agents must check the correct product is selected in the ticket so that it goes to the correct suport team (IOG or NPSG). See ISvC Custom Views Setup for details about filtering by IOG or NPSG products.
 
Most of the times the customer will select the correct product when submitting the ticket; but chances are that the product is not correct based on the customer's issue description or the support ticket is created with the generic product Memory and Storage (which by default will be visible in the NPSG custom view). The agents must ensure the correct product is selected every time a new support ticket arrives to the default ICS Memory and Storage L1 queue.

Community Cases
The support teams are still expected to follow the general case handling guidelines for communities from the Process_WW_Intel Communities Case Handling article. The information shown here only explains how to properly identify the cases that come from the community forums.
 
Products
There are currently four different community forums for SSDs & Memory products. When a new thread is created in one of those community forums, a new support ticket is created within ISvC under the default ICS Memory and Storage L1 queue with a default product selected as shown below:

Since the system is not able to know the specific SSD model of the new threads posted in the Solid State Drives community forum, the generic product Memory and Storage is selected. When the support tickets are created, they will be visible in the NPSG custom view (see ISvC Custom Views Setup). The NPSG supporting agents must update the product to the correct SSD model so that the support ticket is properly visible either by the IOG supporting agents or by the NPSG supporting agents in their respective custom views.
 
Labels
Additionally, since the Solid State Drives community forum is intended for all SSDs (IOG and NPSG), the supporting agents must add the following label to each new thread posted in this forum to accurately identify the SSD type. This label will be used for reporting purposes. The label to use in each case is the following:

  • Note: Other products such as Intel® Optane™ Memory, Intel® Optane™ Persistent Memory, Intel® Virtual RAID on CPU (Intel® VROC), Intel® Rapid Storage Technology enterprise (Intel® RSTe), etc. have their own community forums, so rather than adding a label for them, the threads must be moved to their proper forum if they were wrongly posted in the Solid State Drives community forum; as explained in the Process_WW_Intel Communities Case Handling article.
How to add a label?

When the customers create a new thread, they can add different labels from an available list of options. After a thread has been created and posted, the supporting agents can also add extra labels as needed:

  1. Go to the thread in the community forum.
  2. Click on the three-dots icon in the top-right corner from the first post (the original post from the customer).
  3. Select the Edit Message option.
  4. From the Edit Message page, select the applicable label.
  5. Click the Post button.
Thread with no label Thread with label

 

 
 
IPS Cases
The support teams are still expected to follow the general case handling guidelines for SSDs & Memory IPS cases from the Process_CR_IPS Case Handling Guidelines for SSDs & Memory Products article. The information shown here only explains how to properly identify the cases that come from IPS.
 
Both, IOG and NPSG supporting agents will continue monitoring the same IPS queues as there won't be any changes in the IPS queues organization (there may be changes in future). Therefore, each support team is expected to work the IPS cases as usual, but focusing only on their specific product scope depending if it is an IOG or NPSG supporting agent. Refer to the section Products and Queues to see which products are under IOG and NPSG scope.
  • Note: It is important that the support agents (IOG and NPSG) check the case description in the IPS ticket to accurately identify the correct product in question. Sometimes the IPS customers may enter a wrong product when submitting the IPS ticket, so only checking the product field may cause incorrect routings.
When an IPS case has to be transferred to ISvC for further support, the IOG and NPSG supporting agents must double check that the correct product is selected in the ISvC ticket so that the support ticket is properly visible either by the IOG supporting team or by the NPSG supporting team in their respective custom views (see ISvC Custom Views Setup).
 
While it is possible to create custom views within ISvC to easily differentiate the products under IOG and NPSG scope, it is not possible to follow the same approach within IPS because of the following reasons. value.description: Answers to common questions about the Intel® SSD 600p and Intel® SSD Pro 6000p Series.
value.content:
See answers to commonly asked questions about the Intel® SSD 600p Series and Intel® SSD Pro 6000p Series.

Terminology

Abbreviation Term Definition
NVMe* Non-Volatile Memory Express The next-generation specification used to access SSDs through the PCI Express* (PCIe*) bus with greater throughput and lower latency.
PCIe* Peripheral Component Interconnect Express A standard connection found on most systems that supports the high speed of the NVMe SSD.
UEFI Unified Extensible Firmware Interface A specification for system firmware, meant to replace legacy BIOS, that provides software layer between the operating system and the system firmware.
CSM Compatibility Support Module A UEFI firmware feature that enables legacy BIOS-style booting by emulating a BIOS environment.

 

Click or the topic for details:

About

How do I use the Intel® SSD 600p/Pro 6000p Series as a data drive? For optimal NVMe support, we recommend having a UEFI enabled System BIOS.
Confirm the NVMe driver is loaded within the Device Manager > Storage Controllers. Initialize the disk in disk management, format, and use.

 
Note Windows 7* doesn't contain an NVMe in-box driver. You must install the available Microsoft KB Hotfix or the latest Intel® RST driver.
How do I use the Intel® SSD 600p/Pro 6000p Series as a boot drive?Refer to the installation guide for requirements and instructions.
Is RAID a supported configuration using two or more of the Intel® SSD 600p/Pro 6000p drives? Yes, the latest Intel® Rapid Storage Technology (Intel® RST) driver supports RAID. Make sure you use the driver supported by your system configuration as noted on each driver page.


Hardware and software

What form factors are available for the Intel® SSD 600p/Pro 6000p Series? They are available in the M.2 (2280) form factor.
I have an M.2 SSD in my system. Can my system (hardware) support the Intel® SSD 600p/Pro 6000p series drives?The board must support the NVMe* specification and have an M-key M.2 socket enabled for PCIe. See the product brief.
Note Check with your board or laptop manufacturer to confirm compatibility and proper configuration.
Where can I find NVMe drivers for my Intel® SSD 600p/Pro 6000p Series drive?The standard NVMe in-box drivers that come with the operating system support the Intel® SSDs. We don't have a vendor-unique driver for these products. If you have a 6th Generation Intel® Core™ Processor with flexible input/output support in the system BIOS, you can also use the Intel® RST driver.


Operating system

What operating systems (OS) does the Intel® SSD 600p/Pro 6000p Series support as the primary boot drive?Supported operating systems:
  • Windows 7* (64-bit)
  • Windows 8.1* (64-bit)
  • Windows® 10 (64-bit)
32-bit operating systems do not support UEFI.
Is Linux* a supported operating system? No, Linux* is not a supported operating system.
How do I install the Windows 7* OS on the Intel® SSD 600p/Pro 6000p series drives as a boot drive?

Windows 7* doesn't contain the in-box NVMe* driver for the OS installation as Windows 8.1* and later do.

To see the NVMe* drive, depending on the system configuration:

  • Use the Microsoft® KB Hotfix and installation steps.
    Note You may need to add USB drivers to the Windows 7* image. See the installation
    process    .
  • Use the Intel® Rapid Storage Technology (Intel® RST) driver. Install the driver during Windows 7 installation.
    Note This method only works on platforms that support flexible input/output (remapping). These platforms include 6th Generation Intel® Core™ Processors and later.

The installation guide outlines both of these methods.

Can I migrate my operating system to the Intel® SSD 600p/6000p Series drive?You must use the UEFI drivers and BIOS settings with the NVMe devices. Existing OS installations may not have these settings. We recommend a fresh installation.

BACKGROUND SUMMARY


It was discovered that on Intel® SSD 540s, Pro 5400s and E 5400s series 2.5” drives, pin 10 was not connected to the ground. To make the drives SATA compliant, Intel made a no-notify change grounding Pin 10 on all 2.5” drives starting from ww13 (3/31/2017)

 

KEY MESSAGES

  • In Intel® 540s, 5400s Series 2.5” drives, pin 10 was not connected to the ground
  • Pin 10 is not being used for the drive functionality and hence there was no impact to leaving this pin ungrounded
  • In order to make the drive fully SATA compliant, Intel started grounding pin 10 on all 2.5” drives in the Intel® 540s and 5400s series, starting from ww13 (3/31/2017)
  • Since this change does NOT impact any form, fit or functionality of the drive, Intel will implement this as a no-notify change, with a manufacturing cut-in starting from ww13 (3/31/2017)
  • Detailed testing and technical evaluation confirmed that this pin 10 fix will not impact any functionality
    • Functionality tests, Hardware tests and all certifications have passed with this pin 10 fix
Note: Pin 10 does not change functionality directly, but can change the behavior of the Hard Drive Activity light (Pin 11) as this may be associated with Pin 10 by such devices as Hard Drive Trays

 

INTEL® 540S, 5400S SERIES 2.5” Pin 10 Change Q&A

Q: What is the Pin 10 Change?
A: In Intel® 540s, 5400s Series 2.5” drives, pin 10 was not connected to the ground. In order to be SATA compliant, starting from ww13 (3/31/2017), all Intel® 540s, 5400s series 2.5” drives will have Pin 10 grounded. We have done thorough technical evaluation to determine this is a low-risk change as this pin does not impact any drive functionality.

Q:  What kind of drives are impacted?
A: All Intel® 540s and 5400s series (Professional and Embedded) 2.5” drives will be impacted with this change.

Q:  Are M.2 drives affected by this change?
A: NO. This Pin 10 change is applicable to 2.5” drives ONLY.

Q: Will customers see a change in behavior due to this?
A: There is NO direct impact to the drive’s functionality, power or performance.  It is possible, depending on 3rd party usage of Pin10 as ground, that the behavior of the HD Activity light may be affected

Q: How will I know if I have a drive with the Pin 10 grounded or floating?
A: The serial number on the drives will have a date (work week) identifier and all drives that were manufactured with ww13 (3/31/2017) will have the pin 10 fix in them.  Please contact your Intel Representative for more information on how to determine this

Q: Should the current drives I have be returned?
A: There is no reason to return the drives that have already been deployed in the field, as there is no impact to functionality, power or performance of the drives. All existing drives can be used just as they are.

Q: Will Intel warranty still cover my current drives?
A: Pin 10 change will have no impact to the drive’s warranty. Intel will continue to support warranty on the current drives.

Q:  Will Security or Pro-features be impacted?
A: There is NO impact to any functionality, form or fit to Intel® 540s, 5400s series drives because of this change. Pin 10 is not used for any functionality and hence there is no impact on drive’s functionality because of this change.

Q:  Will the drive’s power or performance be affected?
A: There is no impact to the drive’s power and performance due to this change. The drive will function and perform as expected. This change will be transparent to the drive’s functionality. 

Q:  Why is Intel making this change now?
A: Intel is making this change to make the drives SATA-compliant.  Intel is making every effort to ensure that the drive is fully compliant, even though this change has no impact to the drive's functionality

Q: How did we pass SATA IO certification before if the drive was not SATA compliant?
A: Pin 10 is not used to drive any IO or functionality of the drive. Hence this pin is not tested during SATA IO functionality.

Q: Is there any impact to SATA IO certification?
A: There is no impact to SATA IO functionality of the drive. Pin 10 is not connected to any Tx or Rx

Q: Do we have to re-certify the drives based on this change?
A: Intel has verified that there is no certification impact to this change. Drive re-certification is not required for this change.

Q: Is there any other technical impact to EMI, ESD from my drives based on this hardware change?
A: Intel has performed thorough EMI and ESD testing with Industry standard requirements and can confirm that there is no impact to EMI or ESD due to this hardware change.

Q: What validation has Intel done to determine this change is low-risk?
A: Intel has performed thorough technical evaluation to determine this is a low-risk change. The following aspects were tested to confirm this:

  • Visual Inspection and Pin 10 grounding check, EMI, ESD, Signal Integrity, Drive functionality

Q: What is the benefit of doing this change?
A: Intel ® 540s, 5400s drives will be fully SATA compliant with this change.

value.content:
This is an internal process article. DO NOT attach to a case!
Attach the appropriate article that captures and solves the customer’s issue.
 
 

1. What is e-Retailer Monitoring Program?

External websites where Intel products are sold often include user-generated content in the form of Q&A or Reviews. ICS is currently monitoring and responding when needed on some popular e-retailer sites.
There are two separate activities for the program:

  • Gather customer's data
  • Analyze, monitor and capture Negative Reviews and low score Star Rating 1, 2 and 3, and respond reviews and questions when necessary as follows: 
    • Low score reviews will be provided directly from Stratifyd
    • For questions, agent to follow the link within the review provided by the Stratifyd Tool.

2. Purpose of the Program 

The goal of the program is to turn customers into Intel Brand Advocates or Brand Ambassadors. Brand advocacy is when a person communicates positively about a brand, spreading their message via word-of-mouth on various channels, such as social media, web forums, review sites, and more. For this particular program, we are focussed on Retailer Websites by performing the following tasks:

  • Gettting a pulse of customer sentiment
  • Gathering, understanding and categorizing data with the purpose of providing valuable market and product feedback to the correspondent BU
  • Respond to Negative Reviews
    • Turn negative perception around: Agents will attempt to turn around dissatisfied customers by providing emotional support so that the customer feels heard, by looking for opportunities to delight unhappy customers, by protecting Intel brand, by building a Customer-Care positive reputation and by seizing the opportunity for improvement. 
  • Ensure our portfolio of customer support options is working to alleviate any issue

3. Covered Retailers

India Contact Center:

  • Amazon: Contact Center to use Stratifyd captured data 
  • Best Buy: Contact Center to use Stratifyd captured data 
  • Newegg: Contact Center to use Stratifyd captured data 
  • Microcenter: Contact Center to use Stratifyd captured data 
  • Scan: Contact Center to use Stratifyd captured data 
  • B&H: Contact Center to use Stratifyd captured data 
  • Staples: Contact Center to use Stratifyd captured data 
  • Magazine Luiza (Magalu): Contact Center to use Stratifyd captured data 
  • Microsoft Store: Graphics only, Contact Center to follow manual process, Stratify tool doesnt crawl Microsoft Store 

Shanghai Contact Center:

  • JD: Contact Center to use Stratifyd captured data, capture only Intel Flagship data, do not include other stores.
  • T-Mall: Contact Center to use Stratifyd captured data 

4. Necessary Tools

4.1 Lastpass

  • All agents and SMEs involved need to access the e-Retailer sites via Lastpass only.
  • Getting access: 
    • Contact Center SME emails ics.social.care@intel.com to apply for access (give Name and Email).
    • ICS Social Care will send request to Social Support to invite ICS member.
    • Agent needs to install Lastpass browser plugin and login.
    • Per need basis: It is SME’s role to inform ICS Social Care for agent access removal when the agent leaves the organization.
  • Video tutorial: Lastpass Tutorial
  • Plug-in Installation: Lastpass Plug-in
  • Once plug-in is installed and access is allowed, the agent should see the following: 

4.2 Stratifyd 

  •  URL: https://intel.stratifyd.com/explorer.html?mode=dashboards

4.3 e-Retailer ISVC App

  • App is available within Salesforce Intel eRetailer Monitoring.

5. Gathering, Tracking, Analyzing Data Placement from the e-Retailer Site

5.1 Stratifyd

  • Login into Stratifyd tool and go to the latest Dashboard
  • Select the correspondent e-Retailer (see multiple taps at the top of the dashboard)
  • Go to the right hand side menu and select Stories
  • Select applicable Story (one at a time). For Contact Center purposes use the following stories:
    • Negative Reviews Story: it will display only Negative Reviews excluding 1,2 and 3 Star Ratings
    • 1-3 Star Ratings Story. It will display 1, 2 and 3 Star Rating reviews

  • Click apply. The dashboard will refresh based on the filter applied by the Story
    • Note: Make sure you run one Story at a time and but remove any previous filtering before applying another Story

  • Stories are pulling data for the last 7 days, update the date field for the appropiate date range. Contact Center to monitor previous week at the time. 
  • Click on Data tab at the top of the Dashboard, a list of filtered reviews based on the Story will display

OEM SSD warranty process
value.description: This is a warranty process regarding OEM SSD
value.content:
This is an internal process article. DO NOT attach to a case!
Attach the appropriate article that captures and solves the customer’s issue.


Key Considerations:
1. Intel® can no longer process RMA requests for OEM drives. This is effective July 9, 2016.
2. Troubleshooting is still provided just as it would be for a retail drive. However, if the troubleshooting leads to, or the customer requests an RMA, they will need to be referred to their OEM or place of purchase.
3. If we were to replace those OEM drives with an Intel generic drive then, the customization features included in the OEM firmware will be missing therefore, we may get impacted due to concerns from our customers in regard to possible functionality issues. Hence, the decision from the SSD Business Unit Management is to redirect those RMA customers to their OEM or place of purchase.
4. No additional support is provided for Dell drives as Intel-Dell page has been EOLed. Please follow standard OEM RMA process/guidelines for OEM case handling.
 
 
Handling Procedure:
1. Customer contacts ICS to request support for NAND SSD product(s).

2. Level 1 Agent gathers customer and product details to create an ISvC case (if not yet available).

3. Level 1 Agent determines that the customer has an OEM NAND SSD.

4. Level 1 Agent identifies support request (warranty or technical support).
4.1. For technical support, troubleshoot the product (except for EOIS), but if it turns out for replacement, proceed to Step 4.2.
4.2. For warranty support, ask the customer to go back to their OEM, only if the drive was purchased within the last year and remind him that Intel does not support OEM drives because OEM drives may have different firmware and configuration compared to boxed SSD. If the drive was purchased more than 1 year ago, proceed to Step 5.
4.2.1. If the customer agrees, close the case. End.
4.2.2. If the customer insists on getting a replacement, proceed to Step 5. Note that if the customer falls under any of the EHM criteria, follow article ID 50053.
 
5. Level 1 Agent asks the customer to provide POP.
Note: When asking customer to provide POP, set customer expectation that by providing POP to Intel, he agrees that Intel may contact the issuer (point of purchase) for validation.
  • If the customer asks why we are asking for POP, advise him that:
“Since Intel did not sell you the part, it ensures that the point of purchase is aware of the issue and helps establish authenticity of Intel product. If the point of purchase confirms the proof of purchase is not authentic based on their sales records, Intel will deny your request for warranty. You must address the issue with your point of purchase and this is no longer a business matter with Intel." 
 
5.1. If the POP is provided, escalate the case to EHM Level 2 who will refer to article ID 59042 (Proof of Purchase or Invoice Validation) to validate the invoice. Go to Step 6.
5.2. If the POP is not provided, reject the request.
5.2.1. If the customer agrees, close the case. End.
5.2.2. If the customer disagrees, escalate the case to EHM Level 2 for approval. Go to Step 6.
 
6. EHM Level 2 identifies the next step.
6.1. If the POP is invalid or the customer fails to provide the POP, reject warranty request and de-escalate the case. Level 1 Agent to contact the customer and close the case. End. Note that if the customer falls under any of the EHM criteria, follow article ID 50053.
6.2. If the POP is valid, approve one-time goodwill replacement and coordinate with Technical L2 SME to get the stocking ID of the boxed SSD replacement. On the case post, indicate that Level 1 Agent must emphasize to the customer the risks and potential pitfalls with Intel replacing an OEM drive then, de-escalates the case to Level 1 Agent. Go to Step 7.
  • If the number of units to replace is more than 3 (4 or more), Technical L2 SME must escalate the case to L3 PSE with the alternate options for approval. If the request is for 3 or less units, Technical L2 SME provides the approval.
7. Level 1 Agent informs the customer that we will provide boxed SSD replacement however, its firmware and configuration may be different from their OEM SSD. Make sure to set the right expectation to the customer that we will not collect the defective unit however, customer needs to do one of the following methods to destroy the drive. Once done, you need to ask the customer to send a copy of the COD or pictures to confirm self-destruction of the drive.
 
What are the acceptable ways to destroy drives? 

Customer can choose to destroy OEM drives in one of the following ways: 
1. Certificate of Destruction: Customer to use authorized facility to destroy the drive and send us a picture of the COD. Note: Customers may be charged for this service. 
2. Drill holes through the drive: Customer to drill holes on the drive keeping the serial number (SN) label intact. Send pictures of the destroyed drive showing the SN for Intel records. 
3. Smash the drive: Customer to smash the drive with hammer while keeping the serial number (SN) label intact. Send pictures of the destroyed drive showing the SN for Intel records. . 

Sample Email Script for the Customer:
 
Dear <Customer Name>,
 
In order to help you replace the defective unit, please send us a certificate of destruction from a specialized data destruction company.
 
Examples of these companies are:
Data-Destruction.com (http://data-destruction.com/hard-drive-destruction/)
DataKillers.com (https://datakillers.com/solid_state_media_destruction/)
DataSecurityInc.com (http://www.datasecurityinc.com/degausser/solidstatedestruction.html)
SemShred.com (https://www.semshred.com/contentmgr/showdetails.php/id/2480)
 
You may contact one of them or any specialized data destruction company in order to get a quote and proceed to destroy the unit. In turn, they will provide the certificate of destruction you require.
 
8. Once the customer provided the COD or pictures of the self-destructed drive, Level 1 Agent creates one-way warranty (OWY) case. For NAND SSD, follow article ID 88025 (Warranty Support Handling for NAND SSD Products). End.

 
Process Monitoring / Management
Quality Process Audit (QA), Case Quality Assessment (CQA), Escalations, I4C, PSat
Refresh Rate of Process
Annually
 
Related Documents:
Article ID 40938 - Process_WW_Warranty General Guideliness
Article ID 39649 - Process_WW_Case Handling General Guidelines
Article ID 50053 - Process_WW_ Escalation Handling Manager (EHM) – Escalation Support
 

Acronyms (Key Terms):

Acronym

Definition

OEM

Original Equipment Manufacturer
Generic/Retail Drive
This is a SKU that contains the "Generic" non custom firmware version. 
  • This is the firmware that we provide on the Intel Support site and through the tools like Intel® SSD Toolbox, Intel® DCT and Intel® FUT 
  • These are the drives that are stocked and available in the Warranty Depot/System
  • These drives may have been bought individually or as part of a system

OEM Drive
In the context of this article, this means a drive that contains a Firmware and Model number that is custom and specific for that OEM (Commonly Dell*, HP* and Lenovo*).  Examples below
  • Generic SKU (Intel® Optane™ Memory H10 - 32GB/1TB Single Pack): Model HBRPEKNX0203A01
  • Custom OEM SKU (Intel® Optane™ Memory H10 - 32GB/1TB Single Pack): Model HBRPEKNX0203AD1

value.description: Details related to NAND SSD support changes due to the sale of Intel NAND SSD business and Solidigm™ commitment to provide support under TSA with Intel.
value.content:
Intel’s NAND Solid State Drive business has been acquired by Solidigm™. Visit the Intel Newsroom for details.

Solidigm is committed to providing Technical and Warranty Support to all their NAND SSD customers during the transition. Intel will continue to provide customer support for Solidigm under Transition Service Agreements (TSAs). In the short term, this approach will facilitate a smooth transition with minimal business disruption. In the longer term, it is expected that Solidigm will design systems, tools, and processes to replace the Intel provided services. For any questions, please contact Customer Support.

Technical Support: All the current offerings for technical support remain unchanged.

Warranty Support: Please take note of changes below to warranty processing:

  1. NAND Solid State Drive warranty case creation via the portal or agent interactive support will not allow combining with other Intel products.
    1. Multiple NAND Solid State Drives can be combined in the same warranty case.
    2. All other Intel products can be combined in a separate warranty case.
  2. A separate return request must be made for NAND Solid State Drives. Shipping documentation (e.g., AWB, Commercial Invoice) and packaging must be prepared separately (i.e., there can be no mixture of NAND Solid State Drives and other Intel products in one carton box.)
  3. Please read your shipping instructions carefully for NAND Solid State Drive products information (incl. ATTN name for the return address) to prevent delays.

For any questions, please contact Customer Support.

Summary
Items to take note before contacting FedEx and how to trace the parcel after delivery.
 
 
Resolution

A notification email including the attachments of the commercial invoice and express bill will be sent to you by Intel. Read it carefully and make sure the below materials are prepared before contacting FedEx.

 

Hello Intel customers,

 

Please check the following information about the warranty case in the letter folder file. 

  1. Commercial Invoice  
  2. Courier bill  
  3. Lithium battery regulatory label (if applicable, see label for details) 

 

Please print 3 commercial invoices and sign all pages in the blank space (in English) and the courier note. 

Then contact FedEx to schedule a pickup time. This folder is only valid for 30 days, so please be sure to schedule a pickup request before that time. Once the dispatcher has come to the door, please provide the dispatcher with the three printed commercial invoices and all FedEx courier slips. 

 

If you are unable to print the data, please contact us and we can print the commercial invoice and courier bill for you. 

Reminder: Be sure to return your product using the return clip file assigned to you by this warranty case. 

This avoids case processing delays caused by your product entering the variance list. 

 

If you need help confirming which folder file should be used, you can contact Intel Customer Support at any time before sending the faulty part. 

 

Since your warranty replacement needs to be carried out through our warehouse in Malaysia, when your product is sent to or from Malaysia, you may encounter customs inspection, and once you encounter customs inspection, FedEx may ask you to provide some personal information, and the cost of customs clearance will be borne by Intel. If you have any concerns, you can consult FedEx Customer Service and thank you for your assistance.
